chunks: He said: And Abdullah ibn Jabla narrated to me from Salma ibn Junah from Hazim ibn Habib, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

My parents have died, and Allah has bestowed upon me wealth and provision. Should I give charity on their behalf and perform Hajj? He replied: Yes. Then he said with his right hand (emphasizing): O Abu Hazim, whoever comes to you and informs you that he washed and shrouded the Master of this Command (the Imam) and shook the dust from his grave, do not believe him.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: Master of the Command (Title for the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Hajj and giving charity for deceased parents in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) validates the practice of performing Hajj and giving charity on behalf of deceased parents, reinforcing the continuity of spiritual benefits for the dead. He then provides a crucial eschatological sign regarding the Imam's occultation: the false claim that the Imam has been washed, shrouded, and buried serves to distinguish the true Imam from those who assert his physical death, thereby preserving the doctrine of his enduring presence.
